dataset_name: NASA Capacitor Electrical Stress Degradation Dataset
source: NASA Ames Research Center, Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE)
original_paper: Celaya, J. R., Kulkarni, C., Biswas, G., & Goebel, K. (2012). Towards A Model-based Prognostics Methodology for Electrolytic Capacitors: A Case Study Based on Electrical Overstress Accelerated Aging. Annual Conference of the PHM Society; and Renwick, J., Kulkarni, C., & Celaya, J. (2015). Analysis of Electrolytic Capacitor Degradation under Electrical Overstress for Prognostic Studies.
observation_count: Multiple continuous charge/discharge cycles and EIS frequency sweeps per component across lifetime (thousands of time-series observations)
static_threshold_rationale: Standard industry datasheet limit per MIL-PRF-62F and Vishay/Nichicon capacitor specifications: End-of-Life defined when Capacitance loss exceeds 20% (Delta C / C0 <= -0.20) or ESR exceeds 200% of nominal (ESR >= 2.0 * ESR0).
latent_risk_proxy_definition: A component is defined as harboring a latent risk if at screening cutoff cycle (t_screen), its parametric drift is within acceptable static tolerance (Pass by Traditional Screening), but it subsequently experiences end-of-life failure or accelerated degradation during remaining operational cycles (t_final).
limitations: Component population is 24 units across 3 voltage cohorts (8 units per condition); requires strict leave-one-group-out or leave-one-component-out cross-validation to prevent data leakage.
Degradation is driven by accelerated electrical overstress rather than multi-axis random vibration or thermal cycling profiles.
Latent defects are manifested through accelerated stress testing rather than naturally occurring semiconductor fab defects, requiring rigorous proxy justification.
